title: Pointwise Kan extensions along inclusions of finite posets in infinity categories
statement: Let $A\subseteq B$ be finite partially ordered sets, with the order on $A$ induced from $B$, and let $j$ be the inclusion. The nerve $N(B)$ has $n$-simplices the nondecreasing chains $b_0\leq\cdots\leq b_n$; similarly for $N(A)$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. Let $\mathcal E$ be an infinity category, meaning a simplicial set with fillers for every inner horn $\Lambda^n_k\subset\Delta^n$, $0<k<n$, where $\Delta^n=N(\{0<\cdots<n\})$ and $\Lambda^n_k$ is the union of all codimension-one faces except the $k$th. Write $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$ for the simplicial set whose $n$-simplices are maps $K\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal E$; its vertices are coherent diagrams, and $j^*$ denotes restriction. For a diagram $H:N(A)\to\mathcal E$ and $b\in B$, set $A_{\leq b}=\{a\in A:a\leq b\}$ and $A_{\geq b}=\{a\in A:b\leq a\}$. A colimit is an object representing the space of coherent cocones by its mapping spaces, and a limit is defined dually; the empty colimit is an initial object and the empty limit a terminal object. If every diagram $H|_{A_{\leq b}}$ admits a colimit in $\mathcal E$, there is a coherent diagram $j_!H:N(B)\to\mathcal E$, with a unit $H\to j^*j_!H$ that is an equivalence, and canonical identifications $(j_!H)(b)\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{A_{\leq b}}H$ compatible with their cocones. Dually, if every diagram $H|_{A_{\geq b}}$ admits a limit, there is a coherent diagram $j_*H:N(B)\to\mathcal E$, with a counit $j^*j_*H\to H$ that is an equivalence, and canonical identifications $(j_*H)(b)\simeq\operatorname{lim}_{A_{\geq b}}H$ compatible with their cones. For every coherent diagram $T:N(B)\to\mathcal E$, the left adjunction has its counit $j_!j^*T\to T$ and the right adjunction has its unit $T\to j_*j^*T$ whenever the indicated extensions exist; together with the displayed unit and counit, these induce natural equivalences of mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}(j_!H,T)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(H,j^*T)$ and $\operatorname{Map}(T,j_*H)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(j^*T,H)$. The extensions can be chosen functorially on the full subcategories of diagrams $H$ satisfying the corresponding local existence conditions, and all four units/counits and the mapping-space equivalences are natural on their respective domains: diagrams $H$ satisfying the corresponding local existence conditions and diagrams $T$ whose restrictions satisfy them. In particular, if $\mathcal E$ admits finite colimits, $j_!$ is a left adjoint to $j^*$ on all diagrams; if it admits finite limits, $j_*$ is a right adjoint to $j^*$ on all diagrams. These are infinity-categorical adjunctions and (co)limits, retaining coherent homotopies. Mapping spaces and equivalences use [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Lurie, Higher Topos Theory (March 10, 2012), Definition 4.3.2.2, Proposition 4.3.2.15, Corollary 4.3.2.16, Proposition 4.3.2.17 and Remark 4.3.2.18, printed pp. 271-272 and 284-285, specialized to full inclusions of nerves of finite posets; the right Kan assertion is the opposite-category statement. Second reader opened the official highertopoi.pdf mirror (HTT.pdf failed to open); not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this coherent infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Regard $B$ as an ordinary category with one morphism $b\to c$ exactly when $b\leq c$. Define a strict functor $U:B\to\mathrm{Cat}$ by $U(b)=A_{\leq b}$ and by inclusion on each $b\leq c$. Its Grothendieck category $K$ has pairs $(b,a)$, $a\in A$, $a\leq b$, with $(b,a)\leq(c,a')$ exactly when $b\leq c$ and $a\leq a'$. The source projection $s:K\to A$ sends $(b,a)$ to $a$. The collage $P$ of [lem-coef-infinity-fiber-colimit-collage] has a second, disjoint copy of $B$, with $(b,a)\to c$ exactly when $b\leq c$, and no arrows from that copy of $B$ to $K$. These rules are transitive and define a poset. Its fiber over $b$ is exactly $A_{\leq b}$, and the fiber diagram $H\circ N(s)$ is exactly $H|_{A_{\leq b}}$. All these are finite ordinary categories; no large slice category has been introduced. The nerve of each of these posets is a quasicategory: an inner $2$-horn is filled by transitivity, and in dimension at least $3$ its faces specify the same ordered list of vertices, which gives its unique filler.

source.place: Agent construction of the Grothendieck diagram and collage realizing fiber-cone assembly

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-fiber-colimit-collage] to $Q=H\circ N(s)$. Its sole colimit hypothesis is precisely the left local-existence hypothesis of the item. Obtain $\overline Q:N(P)\to\mathcal E$ and set $F=\overline Q|_{N(B)}$. For every $b$, the specified arrows $(b,a)\to b$ form a colimit cocone with apex $F(b)$. This constructs a coherent $B$-diagram before making any choices of its individual arrows. The monotone map $A\times[1]\to P$ sending $(a,0)$ to $(a,a)$ and $(a,1)$ to the second-copy vertex $a$ supplies a coherent transformation $\beta:H\to j^*F$. The mixed order condition holds because $a\leq a'$ implies $(a,a)\to a'$.

For $a\in A$, the poset $A_{\leq a}$ has final object $a$: from every $x\leq a$ there is exactly one arrow to $a$, so its mapping space into $a$ is a point. By [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit], $H(a)$, with the cocone whose component at $a$ is the identity, is a colimit of $H|_{A_{\leq a}}$. The fiber cocone from step 2 is another colimit of this same diagram, and its component at $a$ is exactly $\beta_a$. The two colimit mapping-space universal properties give an inverse to $\beta_a$: the maps in both directions are the maps carrying one universal cocone to the other, and their composites correspond to identity cocones. Thus $\beta_a$ is an equivalence. The vertexwise equivalence criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes $\beta$ a coherent natural equivalence.

source.place: Definition 7.3.2.1 and the final-object argument underlying the fully faithful inclusion case

proof.text: Check that $F$ has the canonical pointwise colimit property required for mapping-space restriction. For fixed $b$, the slice $N(A)\times_{N(B)}N(B)_{/b}$ is exactly $N(A_{\leq b})$: an $n$-simplex is a chain $a_0\leq\cdots\leq a_n\leq b$. On its right cone define three functors to $P$, all sending the cone vertex to the second-copy vertex $b$: $C_0(a)=(a,a)$, $C_1(a)=(b,a)$ and $C_2(a)=a$ in the second copy. There are natural transformations $C_0\to C_1$ and $C_0\to C_2$, with components $(a,a)\to(b,a)$ and $(a,a)\to a$, and identity at the cone vertex. All their naturality squares commute in the poset $P$. Applying $\overline Q$, the first transformation has identity components on $H(a)$; the second has components $\beta_a$. Consequently both are equivalences of coherent cone diagrams, by step 3 and [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. The $C_1$ cone is the colimit cone of step 2, so the $C_2$ cone is colimiting too: the cone mapping-space tests are conjugate by these equivalences. The $C_2$ cone is precisely $F$ applied to the canonical slice cocone. This also identifies $F(b)$ with the stated colimit of $H$, with the actual cocone induced by $\beta$ and $F$. The triangles $(a,a)\to a\to b$ and $(a,a)\to(b,a)\to b$ in $N(P)$ supply the required comparison homotopies, including their higher compatibilities.

source.place: Definition 7.3.2.1; explicit agent comparison of the fiber and canonical slice cocones

proof.text:
For arbitrary $T:N(B)\to\mathcal E$, apply [lem-coef-infinity-kan-mapping-restriction] with $\mathcal C=N(B)$, $\mathcal A=N(A)$ and the first diagram $F$. The inclusion is full because $A$ has the induced order, and step 4 verifies the colimit hypothesis at every vertex. Restriction gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}(F,T)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(j^*F,j^*T)$. Precomposition by the equivalence $\beta:H\simeq j^*F$ gives
$$\Phi_{H,T}:\operatorname{Map}(F,T)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(H,j^*T),\qquad u\longmapsto j^*u\circ\beta.$$
Composition with an equivalence has inverse composition with its inverse and the two coherent inverse homotopies. Thus this assertion concerns the mapping spaces, not merely their components. No local-existence condition on $T$ was used.

source.place: Corollary 7.3.6.9, restriction followed by the specified unit

proof.text: Make the choices functorial without presupposing coherence of objectwise selections. Let $D_!\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(N(A),\mathcal E)$ be the full subcategory of diagrams satisfying the left local-existence condition, and let $C_{D_!}\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(N(B),\mathcal E)$ consist of diagrams $T$ with $j^*T\in D_!$. These are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], and restriction gives $r:C_{D_!}\to D_!$. For each $H\in D_!$, steps 2-4 give $F$ and $\beta:H\simeq j^*F$. Existence of local colimits is unchanged by this equivalence: precomposing cocones with an inverse of $\beta$ conjugates their mapping-space universal properties. Hence $F\in C_{D_!}$. Step 5 proves that $\beta$ is a universal arrow from $H$ to $r$, for every target in $C_{D_!}$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion] to obtain $j_!:D_!\to C_{D_!}$ with coherent adjunction unit $\eta$ and counit $\epsilon$. It remains to verify that this functorial choice has our specified pointwise property. Both $\beta:H\to rF$ and $\eta_H:H\to rj_!H$ are universal arrows. Their mapping-space universal properties give maps $F\to j_!H$ and $j_!H\to F$ taking one arrow to the other; their composites take a universal arrow to itself and are therefore homotopic to identities. These maps are inverse equivalences. Their restriction takes $\beta$ to $\eta_H$, so $\eta_H$ is an equivalence. Transporting the canonical slice cocones across $F\simeq j_!H$ makes them colimiting: conjugation on all mapping spaces identifies their universal-property tests. Thus every $j_!H$ has precisely the pointwise formula and the unit-cocone compatibility already proved in step 4.

source.place: Proposition 6.2.6.1 applied to restriction on the stated full subcategories; uniqueness of the two universal arrows checked explicitly

proof.text: The counit of the adjunction from step 6 is defined on exactly $C_{D_!}$, so it is a coherent natural transformation $\epsilon_T:j_!j^*T\to T$ whenever the restriction is admissible. By [lem-coef-infinity-local-adjoint-criterion] it is the adjunct of $1_{j^*T}$, and $j^*\epsilon_T\circ\eta_{j^*T}\simeq1$ and $\epsilon_{j_!H}\circ j_!\eta_H\simeq1$ are its triangle identities. For an arbitrary $B$-diagram $T$, even outside this domain, apply [lem-coef-infinity-kan-mapping-restriction] to $j_!H$: step 6 established its pointwise colimit property. Restriction followed by precomposition with $\eta_H$ gives $\operatorname{Map}(j_!H,T)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(H,j^*T)$. This equivalence is natural in $H$ and $T$ because restriction, coherent composition and the unit are natural. On $C_{D_!}$ it is exactly the adjunction equivalence from the criterion, so it induces the same unit and counit, rather than unrelated comparisons. Its naturality in all $T$ needs no colimits for those $T$.

source.place: Adjunction unit/counit from the local criterion; mapping-space restriction extends the formula to arbitrary target diagrams

proof.text: Apply steps 1-7 to $A^{\mathrm{op}}\subseteq B^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$, and then take opposites. Reversing a chain identifies $N(B^{\mathrm{op}})$ with $N(B)^{\mathrm{op}}$; a coherent diagram is sent to its opposite. The lower fiber for $b$ is $(A_{\geq b})^{\mathrm{op}}$, so its colimit in $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ is the required limit in $\mathcal E$. The left unit becomes the equivalence $j^*j_*H\to H$, and the left counit becomes $T\to j_*j^*T$. For the right mapping-space assertion in the fixed right-pinched convention, apply [lem-coef-infinity-kan-mapping-restriction] directly with first diagram $T$ and second diagram $j_*H$. Its right-hand hypothesis is exactly the canonical limit-cone property just obtained by duality. Thus restriction gives $\operatorname{Map}(T,j_*H)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(j^*T,j^*j_*H)$. Postcompose with the counit equivalence $j^*j_*H\to H$; postcomposition with its inverse gives the inverse equivalence. This proves the natural equivalence $\operatorname{Map}(T,j_*H)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(j^*T,H)$, with the specified cones and the dual triangle identities. The reversal of the constructions is definitional duality; the mapping-space conclusion uses the cited right-hand criterion, with no literal identification of left- and right-pinched models required.

source.place: Remark 7.3.2.2: the opposite-category dual, with all domains and maps reversed

proof.text: A finite poset $V$ has only finitely many nondegenerate nerve simplices: these are the strictly increasing chains, of length at most $|V|$, and there are finitely many such chains. Hence all the nerves of $A_{\leq b}$ and $A_{\geq b}$ are finite simplicial sets. If $\mathcal E$ admits finite colimits, then $D_!$ is the whole $A$-diagram category, so $C_{D_!}$ is the whole $B$-diagram category and steps 6-7 give $j_!\dashv j^*$. Finite limits give $j^*\dashv j_*$ by step 8. When $A$ is empty the fiber cones are empty: step 2 requires initial objects, and its dual terminal objects, exactly as stated. When $B$ is empty the only diagram is empty and the constructions are identities; when $A=B$ the fiber posets have final/initial vertices and the units/counits above identify both extensions with the identity.
